story: In April 1789, a shocking mutiny erupted aboard the Royal Navy merchant ship HMS Bounty in the South Pacific Ocean. Disaffected crewmen led by acting-Lieutenant Fletcher Christian seized control from their commander, Lieutenant William Bligh. Rejecting strict discipline after a luxurious five-month layover in Tahiti, the mutineers cast Bligh and eighteen loyalists adrift in a 23-foot open launch with meager rations. Defying all odds, Bligh navigated the overloaded boat across 3,500 nautical miles of dangerous open ocean to reach safety in Timor 47 days later. Meanwhile, Christian sailed the Bounty to remote Pitcairn Island. To ensure no one could ever escape or reveal their hiding place, the mutineers deliberately burned their own warship to the waterline in January 1790, leaving the survivors completely stranded in paradise.
angle: The mutineers sailed to a remote island and deliberately burned their own ship to the waterline so no one could ever escape.
